speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with generalized fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any recent changes in your urine or stool color, such as dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) is a strong candidate given the demographic (middle-aged female is typical, but male presentation occurs), chronic pruritus, fatigue, and history of autoimmune disease (UC), though the age and male gender also raise suspicion for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) or viral hepatitis. Given the sexual history and UC, I must rule out Hepatitis B/C and consider drug-induced causes. To confirm, I will order specific serology and imaging.

REQUEST TEST: AMA_Microsomal_Antibodies, ASAT, ALAT, Alkaline_Phosphatase, Total_Bilirubin, Hepatitis_B_surface_antigen, Hepatitis_C_antibody.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
